primitives.name: Qualified Running Back Count
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Check vs the post — qualification count MATCHES.** The chart states 39 qualified RBs; from public data, min 45 attempts yields exactly 39 qualified RBs this window (a 50-attempt floor yields the same 39 — no RB sits between 45 and 50 attempts).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'N_{qual}': 'Number of qualified running backs (dimensionless)', 'attempts': 'Total rushing attempts (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: A fixed minimum attempt threshold defines qualification; no player lies between 45 and 50 attempts.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure when fewer than 39 players meet 45-attempt criterion.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a discrete set selection operator over player eligibility.
layer2.telemetry: Count of RBs meeting 45-attempt threshold from nflverse

primitives.name: Designed Run Filter
primitives.verbatim_quote: Window: Weeks 1-7, nflverse play-by-play, designed runs only (rush_attempt == 1, 2pt excluded), roster-listed RBs.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F_{design}': 'Set of designed runs (dimensionless)', 'rush_attempt': 'Binary indicator for rush attempt (dimensionless)', 'points': 'Points scored in play (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Only designed runs (not scrambles or trick plays) are considered; 2-point plays are excluded.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Invalid when non-binary rush attempt flags exist or 2-point plays are included.

layer2.mapping: Filters out non-designed rushing plays to isolate intentional ground attacks.
layer2.telemetry: Filtered play dataset from nflverse with rush_attempt=1 and points≠2

It assumes that EPA values are additive and independent, enabling summation across plays. The derived kernel is conditioned on a minimum attempt threshold (45) to ensure statistical significance. The 'qualified_rb_count' primitive acts as a selector function, isolating players who meet the 45-attempt criterion, ensuring a stable sample size. This is critical because the count of 39 qualified RBs matches empirical data, validating the filtering mechanism. The 'designed_run_filter' ensures that only planned rushing attempts are evaluated, excluding scrambles or trick plays. This filter is essential for maintaining consistency in evaluating true rushing efficiency. Together, these primitives form a coherent framework for assessing RB performance under controlled conditions. Failure modes include insufficient attempts leading to invalid counts or inclusion of non-designed runs skewing EPA estimates.
